{{Short description|Type of surface patch used in computer graphics}}
[[Image:Example of coons surface.svg|thumb|400px|right|Sample Coons patch]]

In [[mathematics]], a '''Coons patch''', is a type of [[surface patch]] or [[manifold]] [[Parametrization (geometry)|parametrization]] used in [[computer graphics]] to smoothly join other [[Surface (topology)|surface]]s together, and in [[computational mechanics]] applications, particularly in [[finite element method]] and [[boundary element method]], to mesh problem domains into elements.

Coons patches are named after [[Steven Anson Coons]], and date to 1967.<ref name="coons-tr-41">{{cite book |last1=Coons |first1=Steven A. |title=Surfaces for Computer-Aided Design of Space Forms, MAC-TR-41 |date=June 1967 |publisher=MIT/LCS |location=Cambridge, MA |url=https://hdl.handle.net/1721.1/149362 |access-date=2 June 2024 |ref=coons-tr-41}}</ref>

==Bilinear blending==
Given four [[space]] curves ''c''<sub>0</sub>(''s''), ''c''<sub>1</sub>(''s''), ''d''<sub>0</sub>(''t''), ''d''<sub>1</sub>(''t'') which meet at four corners ''c''<sub>0</sub>(0) = ''d''<sub>0</sub>(0), ''c''<sub>0</sub>(1) = ''d''<sub>1</sub>(0), ''c''<sub>1</sub>(0) = ''d''<sub>0</sub>(1), ''c''<sub>1</sub>(1) = ''d''<sub>1</sub>(1); [[linear interpolation]] can be used to interpolate between ''c''<sub>0</sub> and ''c''<sub>1</sub>, that is

:<math>L_c(s,t)=(1-t) c_0(s)+ t c_1(s) </math>

and between ''d''<sub>0</sub>, ''d''<sub>1</sub>

:<math>L_d(s,t)=(1-s) d_0(t)+ s d_1(t) </math>

producing two [[ruled surface]]s defined on the unit square.

The [[bilinear interpolation]] on the four corner points is another surface

:<math> B(s,t) = c_0(0) (1-s)(1-t) + c_0(1) s(1-t) + c_1(0) (1-s)t + c_1(1) s t. </math>

A '''bilinearly blended Coons patch''' is the surface

:<math>C(s,t)=L_c(s,t)+L_d(s,t)-B(s,t). </math>

==Bicubic blending==
Although the bilinear Coons patch exactly meets its four boundary curves, it does not necessarily have the same [[tangent plane]] at those curves as the surfaces to be joined, leading to creases in the joined surface along those curves. To fix this problem, the linear interpolation can be replaced with [[cubic Hermite spline]]s with the weights chosen to match the partial derivatives at the corners. This forms a '''bicubically blended Coons patch'''.
